correctness.rationale: For Re(s)>=0 and every order alpha in (0,1], the principal power s^alpha has nonnegative real part. Nonnegative integration therefore gives Re(Psi_omega(s))>=0. A characteristic root would force Psi_omega(s) to equal an eigenvalue of J, which is impossible when J is Hurwitz; s=0 is excluded because a Hurwitz matrix is nonsingular. For the source baseline, an independent scalar equilibrium reconstruction gives the published endemic state and a quartic whose coefficients and two nontrivial Routh-Hurwitz margins are strictly positive. The packaged checker recomputes the equilibrium residuals, Jacobian, coefficients, and margins.

originality.rationale: The general distributed-order root criterion is prior work and is not claimed as new. The motivating 2026 paper derives that criterion for its model but reports only finite numerical memory scans. The inspected 2011 general paper and 2013 review do not state or apply the positive-real half-plane obstruction to obtain a Hurwitz-implies-all-memory theorem for orders at most one, and neither certifies the 2026 SEIRS baseline Jacobian. The accepted claim is limited to this exact robust corollary plus the source-specific Hurwitz certificate.
residual_risks: The positive-real half-plane lemma is elementary once the 2011 characteristic-root theorem is known; a mathematically equivalent corollary could exist in distributed-order control literature not surfaced by the inspected searches.
The source-specific numerical Jacobian certificate depends on the printed baseline parameter vector; a different hidden numerical parameter choice would require recomputation.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The motivating paper devotes a full stability-switching analysis and numerical experiments to determining whether changing the distributed-order memory can alter endemic stability. The new result replaces that finite search, at the published baseline, with an exact all-density/all-support theorem: once the ordinary endemic Jacobian is certified Hurwitz, common memory of orders at most one can change transient decay but cannot destroy local stability. This directly sharpens the interpretation of the paper's central numerical conclusion and supplies a reusable diagnostic for the same modeling architecture.
